statement: Max has four 10-cent coins. How many 5-cent coins are worth the same amount?

choices.misconception: I divided 10 by 5 and forgot that Max has four 10-cent coins.
I thought the same number of coins is worth the same amount.
I multiplied 4 by 5 instead of working out how many fives make 40.
I gave the amount of money in cents, not the number of coins.

hints: Find how much money Max has first.
Work out the total amount in cents, then count how many 5-cent coins make that amount. Each 10-cent coin can be swapped for a set of 5-cent coins.
Four 10-cent coins make 40 cents. Count in fives up to 40.

solutions.reliable: Four 10-cent coins are worth 40 cents. Counting in fives, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, takes 8 coins. The idea to keep: change coins into an amount of money before comparing them.
solutions.elegant: Each 10-cent coin is worth two 5-cent coins, so four of them are worth $4 \times 2 = 8$ coins.

whyOnTest: Swapping coins of one value for another checks that the amount, not the number of coins, is what stays the same.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
